reading_scope: Displayed source and targeted change review; helpers and upstream execution not verified
policy: Conservatively reserve every audited component from training; this does not prove all reserved pairs invalid or unreviewed pairs correct.

rows.observation: members is a dict but iteration supplies keys to ban_user; stale user_id is also used for bookkeeping. Missing helper contract prevents confirming repaired safety.
Auth parsing and encoding change requires toString serialization and caller trust boundary; raw auth fields alone do not certify an exploit.
Storage helpers and token comparison change together; their implementations and session binding are missing.
ImportedDump gets an extra filter, but field provenance, filter semantics and exposure route are not shown.
Both paths use escaping; dialect syntax changes do not by themselves prove that one candidate is vulnerable.
Broader permission predicate guards support export; role mapping and contents are needed to establish confidentiality impact.
Missing option terminator is suspicious, but ValidateURL may already reject option-like strings and runcmd behavior is absent.

Both variants test HasPrefix(allowlistEntry, requestedOrg), allowing org abc for entry abcdef/* under ordinary organization semantics. Changing only empty-list policy does not repair this prefix mismatch.
Before embeds key_name in SQL; after parameterizes but prepends its parameter before any lhs parameters. SQL compiler ordering and attacker control require verification.
Prototype-property recursion is suspicious; isObject and mixinDeep behavior are needed to assess the actual pollution paths and completeness of the fix.
New rsync argument validator and insertion position affect safety; its implementation and accepted command shape are absent.
Only update-success bookkeeping changes. A security consequence requires the endpoint-label updater and observer retry behavior.
